title: 中国向银行保障注资450亿美元，市场关注流动性信号
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: A Sunday we've also got China injecting billions of dollars into its banks.
segments.zh: 周日，中国向银行注资数百亿美元。

segments.en: On the one hand, you could say that this should give some confidence, but on the other hand, if this is something you need to do, it doesn't really inspire confidence.
segments.zh: 一方面，这应能提振信心，但另一方面，如果需要这样做，反而难以令人安心。

segments.en: That's a great point. Look, I think with China, specifically, it is in a more classical liquidity trap as an economy,
segments.zh: 说得好。我认为，中国目前更像处于一种经典的流动性陷阱状态。

segments.en: very savings-rich nation, huge current account, and trade surpluses.
segments.zh: 中国储蓄率高，经常账户和贸易顺差巨大。

segments.en: So what is it really doing? I mean, it's injecting capital into its banks.
segments.zh: 那么此举意在何为？实际上，是在向银行注入资本。

segments.en: These banks are holding greater amounts of Chinese government bonds, both state and federal, and those bonds are yielding very low yields.
segments.zh: 这些银行持有大量中国国债，收益率很低。

segments.en: So it's putting pressure on the interest margins for the banking system.
segments.zh: 这给银行体系的利差带来压力。

segments.en: And on the second time, they're injecting capital into the insurance sector and a lot of these insurance companies have relied on higher bond yields in the past.
segments.zh: 同时，向保险业注资，而许多保险公司过去依赖较高的债券收益率。

segments.en: Those are not there anymore. So this could be a sign that they're trying to shore up solvency in the insurance sector.
segments.zh: 如今这些已不复存在，这可能表明他们试图稳固保险业的偿付能力。

segments.en: So it's really just liquidity sloshing around the system, moving in parts of the financial system to shore up investor confidence.
segments.zh: 因此，这实际上只是流动性在金融体系中流转，以稳固市场参与者信心。

segments.en: Might this foreshadow in some way potential rate easing?
segments.zh: 这是否预示着潜在的利率宽松？

segments.en: And if so, what are you expecting in terms of any market impact from this recapitalization?
segments.zh: 如果是，您对这次资本补充的市场影响有何预期？

segments.en: Yeah, that's going to be interesting to follow through here.
